paragraphs.en: As the latest crop of students pen their undergraduate application form and weigh up their options, it may be worth considering just how the point, purpose and value of a degree has changed and what Generation Z need to consider as they start the third stage of their educational journey.
paragraphs.zh: 当新一届学生填写本科入学申请表、权衡各种选择时，或许值得思考：获得学位的意义、目的和价值究竟发生了怎样的变化，以及Z世代在开启教育旅程的第三阶段时，需要考虑些什么。

paragraphs.en: Millennials were told that if you did well in school, got a decent degree, you would be set up for life. But that promise has been found wanting. As degrees became universal, they became devalued. Education was no longer a secure route of social mobility. Today, 28 per cent of graduates in the UK are in non-graduate roles, a percentage which is double the average among the OECD countries.
paragraphs.zh: 千禧一代曾被告知，只要在学校表现出色，取得一个不错的学位，一辈子就有了保障。但事实证明，这一承诺并不可靠。随着学位日益普及，它们也随之贬值。教育不再是实现社会阶层上升的可靠途径。如今，英国有28%的大学毕业生从事不要求大学学历的工作，这一比例是经合组织国家平均水平的两倍。

paragraphs.en: This is not to say that there is no point in getting a degree, but rather stress that a degree is not for everyone, that the switch from classroom to lecture hall is not an inevitable one and that other options are available.
paragraphs.zh: 这并不是说取得学位毫无意义，而是要强调：学位并不适合每个人，从中学课堂迈入大学讲堂并非必然之路，人们还有其他选择。

paragraphs.en: Thankfully, there are signs that this is already happening, with Generation Z seeking to learn from their millennial predecessors, even if parents and teachers tend to be still set in the degree mindset. Employers have long seen the advantages of hiring school leavers who often prove themselves to be more committed and loyal employees than graduates. Many too are seeing the advantages of scrapping a degree requirement for certain roles.
paragraphs.zh: 值得庆幸的是，已有迹象表明这种转变正在发生：Z世代正努力从千禧一代前辈的经历中吸取教训，尽管家长和教师往往仍固守着上大学拿学位的思维。雇主早已看到雇用中学毕业生的好处，因为事实常常证明，与大学毕业生相比，他们工作更投入、对企业更忠诚。许多雇主也正在认识到，取消某些岗位的学位要求具有好处。

paragraphs.en: For those for whom a degree is the desired route, consider that this may well be the first of many. In this age of generalists, it pays to have specific knowledge or skills. Postgraduates now earn 40 per cent more than graduates. When more and more of us have a degree, it makes sense to have two.
paragraphs.zh: 对于希望走获取学位这条道路的人来说，要考虑到，这个学位很可能只是以后许多个学位中的第一个。在这个通才的时代，拥有专门知识或技能会带来回报。如今，研究生学历者的收入比本科学历者高40%。当我们中越来越多人拥有一个学位时，拥有两个学位就变得合乎情理。

paragraphs.en: It is unlikely that Generation Z will be done with education at 18 or 21; they will need to be constantly upskilling throughout their career to stay employable. It has been estimated that this generation, due to the pressures of technology, the wish for personal fulfilment and desire for diversity, will work for 17 different employers over the course of their working life and have five different careers. Education, and not just knowledge gained on campus, will be a core part of Generation Z’s career trajectory.
paragraphs.zh: Z世代不太可能在18岁或21岁时就结束受教育的过程；他们需要在整个职业生涯中不断提升技能，才能保持就业能力。据估计，由于技术带来的压力、实现自我价值的愿望以及追求多样化的需要，这一代人在整个职业生涯中将为17个不同的雇主工作，并从事五种不同的职业。教育将成为Z世代职业发展历程的核心组成部分，而不仅仅是他们在校园里获得的知识。

paragraphs.en: Older generations often talk about their degree in the present and personal tense: ‘I am a geographer’ or ‘I am a classicist’. Their sons or daughters would never say such a thing; it’s as if they already know that their degree won’t define them in the same way.
paragraphs.zh: 年长一代谈起自己的学位时，常常用现在时来界定自己的身份：“我是地理学者”，或“我是古典学者”。他们的子女绝不会这样说；仿佛他们已经知道，自己的学位不会以同样的方式定义自己。
